sources.citation: Stanford, Ronald. 1967. The Bekwarra language of Nigeria: a grammatical description. PhD thesis, School of Oriental and African Studies, University of London. 326 pp. (ProQuest 10673020 digitisation; CORE mirror of SOAS Research Online)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a university library login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 2 'The Transcription and the Tonal System' (thesis pp. 25-38) gives consonants, vowels, tone (syllable = tone-bearing unit; three level tones H/M/L; falling/rising contours analysed as sequences), verb tone classes, pause-group pitch constancy with pre-pausal drop of M/L, 'no significant intonation patterns', emphasis marked grammatically or by vowel/nasal length, word junction and clitic tone. Author states a full phonology is outside the thesis's scope (p. 25). Full-text grep of all 328 pp.: 'stress' occurs only once in the sense 'lay stress on' (syntax), 'accent' only for the…

sources.citation: Stanford, Ronald. n.d. [archived 2014]. Junction features in Bekwarra. Unpublished ms., Institute of Linguistics, 10 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 57017 (draft, posted as is).
